verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is the reporter, not the fault. Every sampled PlaceOrder trace in the degraded window aborts at the checkoutservice -> shippingservice GetQuote hop, the only consistently ERROR-marked downstream call, with the error propagating up to frontend [tr_dde609429310]. It is a fast error, not a wait: GetQuote spans are ~2.5-3.5ms and whole traces finish in 6-11.6ms [tr_dde609429310]. Shipping's own server span and its HTTP child are short and unmarked, so the bad status surfaces at the checkout/shipping boundary rather than from slow shipping processing [tr_dde609429310]. Checkout logs show PlaceOrder entries continuing through 02:49:25 with no downstream completion lines and no error text of its own [tr_3eb575d93fcc]. No dispatch ever queried shippingservice's logs, metrics, or change history, so the mechanism behind the returned error is unestablished — most likely a wrong value on the shipping call path (address, quote backend, or currency/format contract) given a fast deterministic reject with no latency and no checkout-side change [tr_15d52c435af0].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize the failure precisely and consistently across all 12 sampled traces to one hop, and rule out cartservice, currencyservice, productcatalog/featureflag, payment, email, and latency/timeout generally [tr_dde609429310]. checkoutservice itself has no change in or after the window [tr_15d52c435af0] and no error-ratio regression at onset — its error ratio is actually below baseline with an unchanged maximum and change points hours earlier [tr_ea8f741ff321], which argues the checkout binary and config are unchanged and the new behaviour arrives from the shipping dependency. cartservice is exonerated on three fronts: healthy logs through 02:49:26 with no Redis errors [tr_5ff39364ac73], fast unmarked spans [tr_dde609429310], and all fault-injection changes reverted ~1.6h before onset [tr_80c363efc66d]. That leaves shippingservice as the blamed service. I decline to name a fault_class because no evidence was gathered on shippingservice at all: a fast error with no latency rules out dependency_latency for the checkout->shipping hop and argues against resource_exhaustion (no queueing or saturation signature), but bad_config versus bad_deploy on shipping cannot be separated without its change log.
open_questions: No dispatch queried shippingservice logs, metrics, or change history — the actual mechanism and any change record on shipping are entirely unexamined.

Whether the GetQuote error is a returned non-OK gRPC status from shipping or a client-side failure in checkout's handling of a valid response; the trace shows the error only on the checkout-side span.
Onset timing is unpinned: the checkout log query omitted the middle of the window and checkout's error-ratio metric flags no transition at 02:44:45, so nothing localizes the change to that minute.
Whether shippingservice's own upstream (the reqwest-http-client target, likely quoteservice, which also alerted at 02:47:30) is returning bad data that shipping surfaces as an error.

alternatives.root_cause: quoteservice returns invalid or error responses to shippingservice, which shippingservice passes back as a failed GetQuote.
alternatives.why_not: quoteservice alerted at 02:47:30, consistent with this, but its span inside shipping is short and not error-marked in any sampled trace [tr_dde609429310]; blaming it requires a hop nobody queried.

alternatives.root_cause: A checkoutservice-side defect or config in how it constructs or validates the shipping quote request causes a deterministic reject before shipping does real work.
alternatives.why_not: checkoutservice has no recorded change at or after onset [tr_15d52c435af0] and its error ratio shows no regression or step at 02:44:45 [tr_ea8f741ff321], so nothing on the checkout side changed to start this.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected or claimed. The observable that would justify a future action does not yet exist: nothing in the evidence board names a deploy, image change, or configuration edit on shippingservice inside the incident window, and nothing points at process state. The next step is investigative, not remedial — query shippingservice's change history, logs, and error-ratio metric, plus quoteservice's (the reqwest-http-client target that also alerted at 02:47:30), and only then re-open the remediation question.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a dispatch against shippingservice's change history returns a config or image change landing between roughly 02:40 and 02:45 — in that case revert_config or rollback_image on shippingservice becomes proposable with a concrete precondition met, and the expected effect would be the checkoutservice->shippingservice GetQuote span losing its ERROR marking within a few minutes and checkout logs resuming payment/email/message-write completion lines after each PlaceOrder start. It is also wrong if shippingservice turns out to be restart-fixable process state (e.g. a stale cached quote-backend address or exhausted client pool), which would show as shipping-side error logs naming connection or parse failures. Neither observation exists on this board.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible PlaceOrder failure at the frontend for as long as the investigation takes — the fault is live through 02:49:25 and every sampled trace aborts. The risk of not abstaining is worse and specific: the three candidate mechanisms (bad address, wrong quote backend, currency/format contract mismatch) are distinguished by evidence nobody has collected, so any of the permitted actions would be a guess. rollback_image or revert_config on checkoutservice in particular is affirmatively contraindicated — checkout has zero recorded changes from onset forward and its error-ratio metric flags no transition at 02:44:45, so there is no prior state to roll back to and recreating the container would reset a healthy reporter while leaving the shipping-boundary error intact. A restart_service on shippingservice would discard cache, briefly reset connections for its callers, and, if it accidentally cleared the fault, destroy the evidence needed to explain it.
proposal.blast_radius: No services touched. For the record, had an action been proposed the reachable targets and their observers would be: shippingservice (called by checkoutservice on the GetQuote path, itself reached from quoteservice; a recreate resets connections seen by checkout and cascades to frontend and loadgenerator), checkoutservice (called by frontend, which is already ERROR-marked end to end and would additionally see connection resets), and quoteservice (shipping's own upstream, which alerted at 02:47:30). accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, currencyservice, and cartservice are in the incident's reach but downstream of the abort point and unaffected either way.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Checkout alerted first and its downstream consumers followed within three minutes, which is a real fan-out pattern rather than a lone warning. No open incident covers it and the trigger could be checkout itself or any of its dependencies, so the fault class stays unknown pending evidence.
